problem_text:
A logistics coordinator needs to assign shipments to identical cargo planes. Shipments:
* Shipment A: volume 50 m³
* Shipment B: volume 31 m³
* Shipment C: volume 53 m³
* Shipment D: volume 32 m³
* Shipment E: volume 57 m³
* Shipment F: volume 31 m³
* Shipment G: volume 66 m³
* Shipment H: volume 70 m³
* Shipment I: volume 65 m³
* Shipment J: volume 31 m³
* Shipment K: volume 33 m³
* Shipment L: volume 33 m³
* Shipment M: volume 56 m³
* Shipment N: volume 69 m³
* Shipment O: volume 49 m³
* Shipment P: volume 58 m³
* Shipment Q: volume 51 m³
* Shipment R: volume 31 m³
* Shipment S: volume 65 m³
* Shipment T: volume 54 m³
* Shipment U: volume 36 m³
* Shipment V: volume 56 m³
* Shipment W: volume 47 m³
* Shipment X: volume 32 m³
* Shipment Y: volume 51 m³
* Shipment Z: volume 32 m³
* Shipment [: volume 33 m³
* Shipment \: volume 52 m³
* Shipment ]: volume 37 m³
* Shipment ^: volume 69 m³
* Shipment _: volume 30 m³
* Shipment `: volume 70 m³
* Shipment a: volume 63 m³
* Shipment b: volume 70 m³

Each cargo plane can carry up to 100 m³ of cargo. Assign all shipments using the fewest planes possible. Each shipment must be loaded onto exactly one plane, and the total volume on any plane cannot exceed its capacity.
